newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas continues retreat on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas continues retreat on mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices fell another 10 to 20 cents Tuesday, pressured by forecasts for above-normal temperatures in more than half of the U.S. this week, industry sources said.

Prices on the Louisiana Gulf Coast pipes softened by about 10 cents to the high-teens to low-$3.20s, with the higher-priced deals evident late. These prices indicate a drop of at least 60 cents from December indices.
Near record-high temperatures in the producing region kept buyers on the sidelines. As a result, prices on the south Texas pipes declined by about 20 cents to the low-$3 area.
Similarly in the market areas, prices at the New York city-gate fell by about 15 cents to about $4.05.
PECO Energy's 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 2 nuclear power unit in Pottstown, Pa., is still shut, and the company said the unit would possibly restart this weekend.

Also, Northeast Utilities reported earlier Tuesday that about 26,400 electricity customers in Connecticut were still without service, down significantly from Monday's tally of 100,000. About 22,000 and 2,800 customers were out of service in New Hampshire and western Massachusetts, respectively.
Temperatures in the Northeast are forecast to climb to about two to five degrees Fahrenheit above-normal Wednesday through Saturday but then return to near-normal by Sunday.
In the Midcontinent, where above-normal temperatures have also taken their toll on heating demand, prices were down almost 10 cents to the $3.15-3.20 range.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices tumbled another 10 cents to the $3.13-3.15 area, with some late buying evident late.
Waha prices also fell by more than 10 cents to the $3.15-3.20 range.
At the southern California border, traders reported closing deals in the mid-$3.30s in light activity, down about 30-40 cents from December's index.
Buyers and sellers were at a standstill, one trader said, since prices had fallen so well below index levels and demand was near nil.
Temperatures are forecast to hover above-normal through the end of the week in the western U.S. but then return to near-normal by the weekend.
